attempts.label: DANDI:002014
attempts.paper_title: Aseptic, semi-sealed cranial chamber implants for chronic multi-channel neurochemical and electrophysiological neural recording in nonhuman primates

inputs.what: The paper's lists of large and small successful trials (1-based ids, files "09272024_nlx_c8c_value object start_big rew and success_tr1-1411.mat" and "..._small rew and success_tr1-1411.mat", md5 d3199b1d6d5d7a2e4e2ce2b23d2cb8bb and 21b6ec1119ff8924a3dd98a8537bbb68), from the Zenodo record the paper's Data availability statement names. Used only to check the trial classes built from the dandiset's events.

attempts.entry_title: Dopamine, spikes and beta LFP from chamber-implanted carbon fiber electrodes (Choi et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: The recordings that demonstrate the chamber held up in this data: dopamine rose more after large than small reward cues, spiking was locked to the value cue, and the single-trial dopamine and unit waveform panels passed, the last on a weak test. The stronger beta-band suppression after large reward cues held only in direction (p = 0.112); the paper does not describe this analysis, so its band and windows here are the reproduction's choices. The paper's results on the chamber itself, recordings in two monkeys, electrode yields, asepsis cultures, drainage and bone growth, could not be tested, because the dataset holds one session of one monkey.
attempts.description: Tests Choi, Amjad, Murray, ... and Schwerdt (2025) on dandiset 002014, which holds one session of monkey T, the session of the paper's Figures 8 and 9. It tests the single-trial and trial-averaged dopamine at site c8ds, the task-aligned spikes, waveform and interspike intervals at site c5d, and the beta-band LFP suppression at c7b referenced to c5c. The electrode yields, cultures, drainage, bone growth and monkey J are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Choi et al. (2025) from dandiset 002014
The earlier attempt's findings, checked on version 0.261120.0528

outcomes.statement: In a single trial (trial 133 of the session), dopamine concentration changes at site c8ds fluctuate, especially after the value cue display.
outcomes.quote: Single trial measurements of dopamine concentration changes (Δ[DA]) as a function of time relative to value cue display (V) at 0 s (trial 133 in the session). ... Δ[DA] fluctuations are especially visible after the value cue display.
outcomes.notes: In trial id 133 (row 132, a large successful trial) the SD of the dopamine trace referenced at V is 4.414 over 0 to 5 s after V and 2.180 over the 5 s before, ratio 2.025. Under the other reading (row 133, a small trial, with 17 and 22 NaN samples in the two windows) the ratio is 2.199. Over the 941 successful trials with a ratio (9 of 950 are NaN) the median ratio is 1.259 (IQR 0.804 to 1.885), 62.7% are above 1, and trial 133 lies at the 0.775 quantile. The referenced trace of trial 133 is printed from 5 s before to 5 s after V; it dips to -1.84 about 1.1 s before V and rises to 13.59 about 1.9 s after. The paper gives no values to compare with. The trial-aligned FSCV lags the raw scans (iox best matches the raw current about 1.5 s earlier, and da follows iox by a further 0.1 to 0.4 s in 13 trials), so part of the rise after V may come from changes in the raw current just before V.
deviations: The stored PCA estimate (`da`, units not given) is used; the paper's color plot of the voltammograms cannot be compared, as the background-subtracted voltammograms of the trial are not in the file.

outcomes.statement: Trial-averaged dopamine at site c8ds, aligned to the value cue, increases more for large than for small reward trials, especially between the value cue display and reward.
outcomes.quote: Trial averaged Δ[DA] aligned to V at 0 s for large and small reward trials, showing increased dopamine release for large in comparison to small reward trials, especially between the value cue display and reward (RW) event.
outcomes.notes: From V to RW the referenced dopamine averages 1.853 in 448 large and 1.095 in 498 small successful trials, difference of means 0.758, two-sided Mann-Whitney p = 0.0028; 4 trials dropped as their window holds only NaN. Variants, RW to RW + 3 s 1.546 (p = 0.00012); 0 to 2 s after V 0.091 (p = 0.57). V to RW in the first half of the session 0.778 (p = 0.051) and in the second 0.745 (p = 0.018). By 1 s windows the large minus small difference is 0.33 or less until 2 s after V, 1.15 to 1.44 from 2 to 4 s, 1.32 from 4 to 5 s and 1.57 to 1.68 from 5 to 8 s (RW is 4.72 to 5.50 s after V). The criterion tests the V to RW window only. On the statement's "especially between the value cue display and reward", the difference arises between V and RW (from 0.33 at 1 to 2 s after V to 1.44 at 3 to 4 s) and is then held at about 1.6; referenced at RW it grows by only 0.19, 0.48 and 0.25 per 1 s window over 0 to 3 s after RW, and the RW to RW + 3 s window is referenced at V, so it carries the difference built up before RW. Only the level of the difference is as large after RW as before. A question to a reader asks whether the criterion should test this part. The trial-aligned FSCV lags the raw scans by about 1.5 s or more (data check), so the null 0 to 2 s variant may in part reflect this delay. The paper reports no test.
deviations: The trace is referenced at V by subtracting the stored estimate's value there, as the criterion says, in place of the paper's background subtraction of the voltammograms at V.

Trials are classed from the events, leaving out the last row (id 1411), which has no next trial start and which the paper's Zenodo lists leave out; this gives the lists exactly (451 large, 499 small).

outcomes.statement: Spikes recorded at site c5d on a chamber-implanted CFE can be shown as a raster and a peristimulus time histogram aligned to the value cue display, for large and small reward trials.
outcomes.source: Figure 9A and its legend; Results, section 3.5, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: Raster plot of spikes detected on each trial (y-axis) as a function of time relative to value cue display (V) at 0 s (site c5d). ... Peristimulus time histogram (PSTH) showing average spike firing rate (y-axis) for the large (red) and small (blue) reward conditions
outcomes.notes: All 950 successful trials have a spike from 1 s before to 3 s after V. The variance across the 40 bins of the PSTH is 0.4807 (spikes/s)^2; the 95th percentile over 200 random alignments is 0.0574 under the claim's seed and 0.0574 to 0.0607 under the seed plus 1000 to 4000, and no random alignment reached the observed value under any of the five seeds. The rate falls to 3.8 spikes/s 0.1 to 0.2 s after V and rises to 7.7 to 7.8 spikes/s 0.3 to 0.5 s after V (baseline about 5.5). V falls at every phase of the FSCV scan cycle (77 to 108 trials per 10 ms bin) and each 100 ms bin spans one whole cycle, so the spike-free gap of each scan cannot make this fall and rise. The stored times (0.4697) and the Plexon unit (0.4829) give the same result. The large and small PSTHs differ by at most 2.03 spikes/s in a bin, mean difference -0.050 spikes/s over -1 to 3 s; the paper states no difference, and none is judged.
deviations: Spike times are moved by the offset measured in the data check, 0.5 ms (raw ephys clock later than the trial clock), not by the 11812.1 s the claims file's opening comment reports for an earlier version of the dandiset; in this version every stream is on one clock.

outcomes.statement: The spikes at site c5d have a consistent waveform (mean and standard deviation) and an interspike interval distribution (1 ms bins) consistent with a single unit.
outcomes.quote: Average spike waveform + /− standard deviation. C. Interspike interval (ISI) histogram showing the distribution of the timing between spikes detected. Bin widths are 1 ms.
outcomes.notes: None of the 101732 interspike intervals of thresholded unit 1 is shorter than 1 ms (shortest 1.562 ms, fraction under 2 ms 0.00008). The mean waveform's largest absolute value is 56.36 uV (negative) at sample 10 of 48, 4.79 times the SD across spikes at that sample (11.76 uV); 4.78 and 5.05 in the two halves of the session. The refractory test cannot fail on these spikes, as the shortest interval is about the waveform length (1.50 ms), so the detector may not report a second spike within one waveform. The Plexon unit has 2 intervals under 1 ms (0.00002). Both tests of the criterion hold, so the outcome is reproduced; that the unit is a single neuron is not shown by them, and the paper does not state it (the claim's statement does); a question to a reader asks whether the statement and criterion should change.

outcomes.statement: Trial-averaged beta-band LFP power at c7b referenced to c5c is suppressed more in the brief window after the value cue for large than for small reward cues.
outcomes.quote: Trial averaged beta-band LFP power showing increased suppression during the brief time window immediately following the cue (V) for large as compared to small reward cues (site c7b-c5c).
outcomes.notes: Median log10 ratio of 13 to 30 Hz power over 0 to 0.5 s after V to the 0.5 s before is -0.156 in 451 large and -0.125 in 499 small trials, difference of medians -0.031, two-sided Mann-Whitney p = 0.112; no trial dropped. Both medians are below 0 and large is lower, with p >= 0.05, which the criterion calls partially reproduced. Variants with the N = 4 filter, 0 to 0.3 s -0.0001 (p = 0.59), 0 to 1 s -0.008 (p = 0.83), 1 s baseline -0.023 (p = 0.12), 15 to 30 Hz -0.027 (p = 0.066), 12 to 25 Hz -0.021 (p = 0.20). With N = 2 the 15 to 30 Hz band gives -0.035 (p = 0.052) and the others p 0.11 to 0.81. First half of the session -0.183 against -0.134 (p = 0.116), second half -0.126 against -0.115 (p = 0.545). The trial-averaged power ratio dips lower for large trials (to 0.532, against 0.695; mean over 0 to 0.5 s 0.841, against 0.885), which resembles the paper's figure; the criterion compares medians of the per-trial log ratios.
deviations: The 4th order Butterworth band-pass of the criterion is designed with N = 4 (scipy's and MATLAB's convention, a standard choice); N = 2 is shown as a variant.

The stored LFP is used, as the criterion says. It equals the raw c7b minus c5c except at the FSCV scan rate (10 Hz) and its harmonics, which dominate the raw signal and are removed from the stored one (data check, spectra); this is why it carries only 0.14 to 0.17 of the raw SD in 13 to 30 Hz. The beta band thus has gaps at 20 and 30 Hz. The paper's preprocessing is not described; the Zenodo record calls it spectral interpolation.

outcomes.statement: The chamber system provided recordings of dopamine and electrical neural activity in two monkeys (T and J).
outcomes.quote: Our chamber system was shown to provide successful recordings of dopamine and electrical neural activity in two monkeys
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds one session of monkey T, with dopamine (c8ds), spikes (c5d) and LFP (c7b-c5c), so the monkey T part is present. No recording of monkey J is in it, in the paper's Zenodo record (one session of monkey T), or in any other dandiset or Zenodo record of the lab found by searching both archives for Schwerdt (dandiset 002013 is another study).

outcomes.statement: 53% (21/40) and 25% (13/51) of implanted sCFEs retained functionality (background current above 500 nA and noise below 0.05 nA) in monkeys T and J.
outcomes.quote: 53 % (21/40) and 25 % (13/51) of the implanted sCFE’s retained functionality (background current > 500 nA and noise < 0.05 nA) in monkeys T and J, respectively.
outcomes.notes: The background current and noise of each implanted electrode are not in the dandiset or the Zenodo record. The file holds one FSCV electrode (c8ds).

outcomes.statement: 73% (29/40) and 39% (20/51) of implanted sCFEs retained background current above 500 nA in monkeys T and J, of which 28% and 35% had noise above 0.05 nA.
outcomes.quote: 73 % (29/40) and 39 % (20/51) of the implanted sCFE’s retained viable background current > 500 nA, and of these several (28 % and 35 % in monkeys T and J, respectively) fell short of full functionality with noise levels > 0.05 nA.
outcomes.notes: As for scfe-functional-yield, the per-electrode background currents and noise levels are not public.

outcomes.statement: 21.4% (3/14) and 14.2% (2/14) of mCFEs retained functionality in monkeys T and J.
outcomes.quote: On the other hand, the mCFE’s retained a lower functional yield of 21.4 % (3/14) and 14.2 % (2/14) in T and J, respectively.
outcomes.notes: The per-electrode functionality of the mCFEs is not in the dandiset or the Zenodo record.

outcomes.statement: Of the functional CFEs, 63% (15/24) and 53% (8/15) in monkeys T and J displayed visible dopamine signals and were used during task performance.
outcomes.quote: Of the functional CFEs, 63 % (15/24) and 53 % (8/15) in monkeys T and J, respectively, displayed visible dopamine signals (i.e., current changes along dopamine redox potentials), and were successfully applied in measurements during task performance.
outcomes.notes: Only one FSCV site (c8ds) of one monkey is in the dandiset; the 24 and 15 functional CFEs are not.

outcomes.statement: Monkey T kept negative bacterial cultures for all samples; in monkey J, staphylococcus cultured at 29 days post-implant was cleared by 39 to 44 days and the chamber stayed aseptic for 286 days after treatment.
outcomes.quote: Bacteria (staphylococcus) was cultured about a month post-implant (29 days) in monkey J ... Monkey T maintained negative cultures for all collected samples. ... 39 – 44 days post-implant the samples began to show negative results ... maintained aseptic condition for the next 286 days
outcomes.notes: The culture results are not in the dandiset or the Zenodo record.

outcomes.statement: Fluid aspirated from the chamber per session ranged from 0.3 to 4.8 mL in monkey T and 0.2 to 9.8 mL in monkey J, and was sanguinous for the first 18 (T) and 217 (J) days.
outcomes.quote: Fluid collected from the chamber aspiration tube for a given day varied between 0.3 – 4.8 mL for monkey T and between 0.2 – 9.8 mL for monkey J (Fig. 6). ... sanguinous (i.e., bloody) in the first few weeks or months (18 days post-implant in monkey T and 217 days in J)
outcomes.notes: The aspirated volumes are not in the dandiset or the Zenodo record.

outcomes.statement: Bone growth was observed within and around the chamber in both monkeys, and the chamber margins stayed relatively healthy.
outcomes.source: Results, section 3.3, paragraph 1, and section 3.4, paragraph 1; Figure 7
outcomes.quote: Prominent bone growth was observed in both monkeys within and around the chamber interfaces (Fig. 7). ... The margins of the chamber in both monkeys remained relatively healthy and intact (Fig. 7D and E).
outcomes.notes: The photographs of bone growth and chamber margins are not in the dandiset or the Zenodo record.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds one session of monkey T (09/27/2024), the session of Figures 8 and 9. The electrode yields, cultures, drainage volumes, bone growth and margin observations, and every recording of monkey J are not in it, so 8 of the 13 claims cannot be tested. The version's release notes state this gap.

All streams share one clock. The stored bipolar LFP matches the raw c7b minus c5c in 1 to 8 Hz at a lag of 0 to 1 ms (r 0.89 to 0.94 in four trials, over a search of 5 s either way); the raw c5d trough falls 8 samples after the thresholded spike times, within 2 samples of the stored waveforms' trough (sample 10); the spike-free gap sits 46 to 50 ms after each stored FSCV scan time throughout the session, consistent with the stated mapping of scans to within one scan; the trial-aligned oxidation current follows the raw current near 0.6 V (a fitted kernel over 36 trials is positive from about -2.8 to +0.2 s and largest at -0.2 to 0 s), though smoothed so that it matches the raw current best about 1.5 s earlier (finding 9); the large minus small dopamine difference appears only after V; and the spike rate is modulated at V far beyond random alignments. The offset of 11812.1 s reported by the claims file for an earlier version does not hold in this one (r -0.12 to -0.02 at that offset, 0.89 to 0.94 at 0 to 1 ms).
findings.checked: No finding is rated critical, and it would rate none critical; the clock offset does not hold in this version (cell 5). It noted that "no shift of more than a few tenths of a second" is true of the kernel's peak (lag 0), while cell 8 also shows the detrended correlation peaking with the raw current 1.5 s earlier (median; range 0.8 to 2.5 s), and that the kernel is positive from about -2.8 s (cell 8 prints +0.2 at -2.8 s and +1.3 at -2.6 s), not from -2.4 s.

findings.statement: The PCA-extracted dopamine, pH and motion components and the oxidation current have no units, and their reference window is not given (the file says so). The dopamine values range from -53.6 to 42.4, so their size cannot be compared with the paper's concentration changes.

The bipolar LFP's preprocessing is described in the file as not documented, while the Zenodo record it comes from calls it downsampled after spectral interpolation. The data show what it does to the signal. The raw c7b minus c5c carries lines at the FSCV scan rate, 10 Hz, and its harmonics (440 to 2200 times their neighbours at 10 to 40 Hz); the stored LFP has them removed and otherwise equals the raw signal (spectral ratio 1.03 to 1.05 at 5 to 35 Hz between the lines).

The thresholded spikes have no interspike interval shorter than 1.562 ms, about the length of a stored waveform (48 samples, 1.50 ms), so their interval distribution cannot show refractory violations. The thresholded unit 1 and the Plexon unit ch75#1 hold the same spikes (99.5% of Plexon spikes within 0.1 ms of a thresholded one) and were counted once.
findings.checked: The thresholded and Plexon units share the same spikes; two detections of the same channel are visible as such in the file (cell 3, 0.9949 overlap), so minor is right.

findings.statement: Classing trials from the events gives the paper's Zenodo lists of large (451) and small (499) successful trials exactly, once the last row (id 1411, a large reward with no later trial start), which the lists leave out, is left out. Every midpoint_time equals a trial-start event (code 128) exactly. The first trial-start event (4640.33 s) has no row in the trials table, as the table's description says.
The version's release notes say the eye tracking was re-timed with the raw ephys, but the file holds no eye tracking series.

The trial-aligned oxidation current (iox) is a smoothed version of the raw current near 0.6 V, and the file does not say so. A linear kernel from the raw current to iox, fitted over 36 trials, is positive from about 2.8 s before to 0.2 s after each sample, largest at -0.2 to 0 s, and negative from +0.4 s, and the detrended correlation peaks with the raw current 0.8 to 2.5 s earlier (median 1.5 s). The PCA dopamine estimate (da) follows iox by a further 0.1 to 0.4 s (median 0.3 s, 13 trials with no NaN), so it carries at least the same delay; matched directly with the raw current, da peaks 1.2 to 5.0 s earlier (median 3.1 s, with 5.0 s the edge of the search). Responses in the trial-aligned series are therefore spread over about 2 s after the raw change, and a latency measured on them comes out late by about 1.5 s or more. How the PCA components were derived from the scans is not documented.

The paper says the reward size depends on whether the target is at the top or bottom of the screen. The events code left (117) and right (118) conditions, and both reward conditions occur on both sides (left 233 trials with condition 1 and 499 with condition 2, right 250 and 429), and no event codes the target's vertical position. The reward condition codes 41 and 40 are described as giving the big and small reward, so each trial's reward size is known, but the target position that the paper says sets it is not in the dandiset.

reconciliation.blind_note: The author saw no record, entry, questions, transcript or note of choi-2025-01; the audit lines are links to the pilot notes and the repository's README. Two inputs the protocol gives the author carried a summary of that attempt's results. The dandiset's release notes, read under step 1.1, list the conversion fixes made after "a reproduction attempt" (one clock for all streams, events no longer stored several times, Plexon timestamps, units), and the claims file's opening comment reports the 11812.1 s clock offset found in the earlier data check. The author disclosed both in its report and tested the offset, which does not hold on this version (its finding 2 and the fig9a deviation).

gone.note: The raw ephys now starts at 4612.10 s on the session clock and lines up with the stored LFP at a lag of 1 ms at the first and last trial (r 0.972 and 0.872, earlier_findings.ipynb); choi-2025-02 finds the same over four trials (its finding 2).
gone.statement: The raw ephys and the spike times are not on the clock of the trials, events, LFP and FSCV table. The raw ephys is stored with a starting time of 0 s and a rate, and the spike times count from its first sample. Locating the raw c7b minus c5c signal in the stored LFP puts raw time 0 at 11812.11 s on the trial clock (correlation 0.98 to 1.00 at eight points, drift about 4 ms per hour). Without this correction spikes cannot be aligned to the task. The dandiset description says all data are expressed relative to the start of the Neuralynx recording, which the data contradict.

gone.note: The raw samples now run from 10:06:44 to 15:12:20, ending 3.9 s before the Neuralynx header's close at 15:12:24, and their start 4612 s after the recording was opened accounts for the longer header span (earlier_findings.ipynb).
gone.statement: The absolute times disagree. On the trial clock the raw samples run from 12:06:44 to 17:12:20, while the Neuralynx header gives the recording as opened at 08:49:52 (the session start) and closed at 15:12:24, two hours before the raw samples end. The header span (22952 s) is also longer than the raw samples (18336 s).

gone.note: The raw c5d trough now falls 0.000 to 0.344 ms after the stored spike times on average at the start, middle and end of the recording, close to the stored waveforms' trough at 0.312 ms (earlier_findings.ipynb); the 7.1 ms lag is gone.
gone.statement: The stored spike times of the thresholded units are about 7.1 ms after the spike troughs in raw c5d (in one 300 s segment of 1633 spikes, per-spike trough lags of -7.4 to -6.9 ms from the 10th to the 90th percentile, 98.8% within 0.5 ms of -7.1 ms).

gone.note: The series is no longer described as beta-band, and it carries a conversion of 1.0 in volts (median absolute value 24.2 uV, earlier_findings.ipynb). Its preprocessing, now described as not documented, is choi-2025-02's finding 4, a new finding.
gone.statement: The series "bipolar_lfp_series" is described as beta-band LFP but is broadband with line noise removed. Its values are already in volts, while it carries the raw int16 conversion factor (3.05e-8), which would scale them about 3e7 times too small.

gone.note: The waveforms now hold volts (mean trough -5.636e-05), and the raw FSCV current carries a conversion of 1e-09 to amperes on values around 1000 (earlier_findings.ipynb).
gone.statement: The thresholded spike waveforms are stated in volts but hold microvolts (mean trough about -56), and the raw FSCV current is stated in amperes but holds nanoamperes (values around 1000).

gone.note: The subject, session and experiment descriptions and the keywords now describe this paper's chamber implant and the 09/27/2024 session of monkey T (earlier_findings.ipynb).
gone.statement: The subject description ("Two adult female rhesus monkeys were used for in vivo validation of the s-µIP device"), the session and experiment descriptions and the keyword "micro-invasive neural implant" describe the lab's micro-invasive probe study, not this paper's chamber.

gone.note: The event table now stores 14117 events, 1412 trial starts, with no repeated time and no decreasing step within a label, and the Plexon spike times are sorted (earlier_findings.ipynb).
gone.statement: The event table stores each event once per overlapping 60 s trial window, about five copies of each (7221 stored trial-start events for 1412 distinct ones), and its event times are not sorted. The Plexon units table's spike times are not sorted either.

verifications.reviewed: The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper's full text (PMC13250822). The verifier read the archive's versions and asset lists through the DANDI API and tested the helpers on synthetic inputs (_first_in, _any_in, psth, da_times, value_at, window_mean, lfp_segment, beta_suppression) and the thresholded_waveforms indexing by hand. It had no attempt record and took the claims from the claims file.

paper_notes.statement: The paper describes none of the analyses of Figures 8 and 9 beyond the legends and reports no test of the large against small differences. For Figure 9D it gives no beta band, filter, power measure, baseline or window for "the brief time window immediately following the cue". Questions for the authors, which band, filter and windows were used, and was the difference in Figure 9D tested? Here the claims file's choices (13 to 30 Hz, 0 to 0.5 s against the 0.5 s before V) give a smaller suppression for large than small trials that is not significant (p = 0.112).
